advances: The canonical discounted endpoint energy gives both a harmonic support bound and a parity-dependent optimization of the accepted band argument under only same-parity midpoint log-concavity. The support bound proves a logarithmic dimension loss whenever normalized support is bounded by a fixed polynomial in the integer dimension. It excludes every admissible reweighting of either accepted tree support geometry as a counterexample to that logarithmic bound. The accepted interval-fiber tree family has an exact limiting cutoff score of two, giving sharp logarithmic dependence on normalized support and an exact logarithmic-logarithmic dimension rate. The optimized band estimate preserves the accepted universal bound and gives a collision-probability refinement, while retaining a dimension loss for exactly balanced parities. All lower bounds pass to actual mixed-integer depth through the accepted factor \(1/12\) consumer. Neither an unrestricted logarithmic dimension bound for the scalar score nor the locked conjecture is asserted.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The accepted inputs are the canonical discounted quantities of `c382ad0f37a86dd8`, the actual-body factor-\(1/12\) consumer and midpoint hypothesis from `03f071403cdfc69f`, the exact rooted-tree support, level census, pair reconstruction, and central-binomial estimate from `032423921efad6c8`, and the exact lifted support geometry from `604889294a17d7df`. The endpoint-energy identities under the weaker hypotheses and every new support, rank, band, collision, reweighting, and asymptotic claim are proved above. The two archived research passages served only as motivation and supply no unverified mathematical premise.
proof:
The midpoint hypothesis gives \(\Delta_j(v)\ge0\) on every \(\mathcal U_j\). These sets are finite, even, and contain zero, with \(\Delta_j(0)=0\) and \(\alpha_j(0)=w_j\). At any cutoff \(L\ge0\), the largest curvature value not exceeding \(L\) exists because zero is available. Replacing \(L\) by that value leaves the numerator unchanged and cannot increase the denominator. Thus each \(K_j(w)\) is attained at one of finitely many curvature values, and finiteness of \(A\) proves attainment of \(K(w)\).

We first prove the common discounted-energy identities, with precisely the normalization of `c382ad0f37a86dd8`, under the weaker midpoint hypothesis used here. Finite summation and elementary integration give
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_j
&=\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_j}\alpha_j(v)
\int_{\Delta_j(v)}^\infty\tfrac12e^{-L/2}\,dL\\
&=\int_0^\infty\tfrac12e^{-L/2}B_j^\Delta(L)\,dL\\
&\le K_j(w)\int_0^\infty\tfrac12e^{-L/2}(1+L)\,dL
=3K_j(w),\\
\mathscr R&\le3K(w)W.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
The two moments in the integral are one and two. In particular a curvature-zero pair, including zero displacement, has its entire coefficient retained.

The map \((j,v)\mapsto(j+v,j-v)\) is a bijection from the pairs counted in \(\mathscr R\) to ordered positive same-parity endpoint pairs. Its inverse is \((x,y)\mapsto((x+y)/2,(x-y)/2)\). The midpoint is positive by hypothesis and is integral by parity. At this inverse pair the exact cancellation is
\[
w_{(x+y)/2}\alpha_{(x+y)/2}((x-y)/2)
e^{-\Delta_{(x+y)/2}((x-y)/2)/2}
=\min\{w_x,w_y\}\sqrt{w_xw_y}.
\tag{15}
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathscr R
=\sum_b\sum_{\substack{x,y\in A\\x\equiv y\equiv b\pmod2}}
\min\{w_x,w_y\}\sqrt{w_xw_y}.
\tag{16}
\]
Distinct unordered pairs are counted twice and diagonal pairs once. This identity and (14) will be used for both refinements; no undiscounted reflected-minimum average is substituted for \(\mathscr R\).

Fix a nonempty parity class and abbreviate its decreasing weights by \(a_1,\ldots,a_R\). Its contribution to (16) is
\[
\sum_{r=1}^R a_r^2+2\sum_{r=2}^R\sum_{s<r}a_r\sqrt{a_ra_s}
\ge\sum_{r=1}^R(2r-1)a_r^2,
\tag{17}
\]
because \(a_s\ge a_r\) for \(s<r\). This remains valid for any ordering among equal weights. Summing (17) and using Cauchy-Schwarz over all class-rank pairs gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
W^2
&\le\left(\sum_{b:R_b>0}\sum_{r=1}^{R_b}\frac1{2r-1}\right)
\left(\sum_{b:R_b>0}\sum_{r=1}^{R_b}(2r-1)a_{b,r}^2\right)\\
&\le\mathscr H(A)\mathscr R
\le3\mathscr H(A)K(w)W.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]
Since \(W>0\), (14), (17), and (18) prove the ranked-weight and harmonic lower bounds in (3).

For every integer \(R\ge1\), \(\sum_{r=1}^R(2r-1)^{-1}\le1+\tfrac12\log R\). Indeed, for \(r\ge2\), convexity of \(x\mapsto1/(2x)\) on \([r-1,r]\) implies \((2r-1)^{-1}\le\int_{r-1}^{r}(2x)^{-1}\,dx\). Summing proves the claim, also at \(R=1\). If \(s_A\) parity classes are nonempty, concavity of the logarithm now gives
\[
\mathscr H(A)
\le s_A+\frac12\sum_{b:R_b>0}\log R_b
\le s_A\left(1+\frac12\log(N_A/s_A)\right).
\tag{19}
\]
For \(0<x\le N_A\), the derivative of \(x(1+\tfrac12\log(N_A/x))\) is \(\tfrac12(1+\log(N_A/x))>0\). If \(N_A\ge2^n\), use \(s_A\le2^n\) in (19). If \(N_A<2^n\), use \(s_A\le N_A\), obtaining \(\mathscr H(A)\le N_A<2^n\). These two cases give the normalized-support bound in (3), including supports smaller than \(2^n\).

If \(N_A/2^n\le(n+2)^a\), then
\[
1+\tfrac12\log_+(N_A/2^n)
\le1+\tfrac a2\log(n+2)
\le\left((\log3)^{-1}+a/2\right)\log(n+2),
\]
which proves (4). To prove (5), the support bound supplies
\[
\log(n_i+2)\frac{2^{n_i}K(w^{(i)})}{W_i}
\ge\frac{\log(n_i+2)}{3(1+\tfrac12\log_+\tau_i)}.
\tag{20}
\]
If the left side tends to zero, the positive right side tends to zero. Hence \((1+\tfrac12\log_+\tau_i)/\log(n_i+2)\to\infty\). Since \(\log(n_i+2)\ge\log3\), subtracting the bounded term \(1/\log(n_i+2)\) proves (5). It follows that \(\log_+\tau_i\to\infty\), so eventually \(\log_+\tau_i=\log\tau_i\). For fixed \(a\ge0\),
\[
\log\frac{\tau_i}{(n_i+2)^a}
=\log(n_i+2)\left(\frac{\log\tau_i}{\log(n_i+2)}-a\right)\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
proving the stated superpolynomial condition.

We next prove the independently optimized parity bound. In a nonempty class \(b\), choose a maximum-weight site \(a_b^{\max}\) and put \(m_b:=w_{a_b^{\max}}\). The site \(a_b^{\max}\) is distinct notation from the ranked scalar weights \(a_{b,r}\). The midpoint map \(z\mapsto(z+a_b^{\max})/2\) is injective within this class, and its images belong to \(A\). Therefore
\[
\sum_{\substack{z\in A\\z\equiv b\pmod2}}\sqrt{m_bw_z}
\le\sum_{\substack{z\in A\\z\equiv b\pmod2}}w_{(z+a_b^{\max})/2}
\le W.
\tag{21}
\]
No injectivity across different parity classes is used. For any integer \(k_b\ge1\), a weight with \(0<w_z\le4^{-k_b}m_b\) satisfies \(w_z\le2^{-k_b}\sqrt{m_bw_z}\). Thus the discarded mass in this class is at most \(2^{-k_b}W\).

Partition the retained sites into the \(k_b\) disjoint bands
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{b,r}&:=\{z\in A:z\equiv b\pmod2,\ 4^{-(r+1)}m_b<w_z\le4^{-r}m_b\},\\
U_{b,r}&:=\sum_{z\in A_{b,r}}w_z
\quad(0\le r<k_b).
\end{aligned}
\tag{22}
\]
The strict lower and weak upper inequalities account for every band endpoint. Their total mass is at least \(W(\pi_b-2^{-k_b})_+\), so
\[
\sum_{r=0}^{k_b-1}U_{b,r}^2
\ge\frac{W^2(\pi_b-2^{-k_b})_+^2}{k_b}.
\tag{23}
\]
Within a band the ratio of endpoint weights is at most four. For positive \(u,v\) with this property, \(\min\{u,v\}\sqrt{uv}\ge uv/2\), because \(\sqrt{\max\{u,v\}/\min\{u,v\}}\le2\). Retaining only same-band ordered pairs in the nonnegative sum (16) consequently gives
\[
3K(w)W\ge\mathscr R
\ge\frac12\sum_{b:R_b>0}\sum_{r=0}^{k_b-1}U_{b,r}^2
\ge\frac{W^2}{2}\sum_{b:R_b>0}\frac{(\pi_b-2^{-k_b})_+^2}{k_b}.
\tag{24}
\]
Thus no second endpoint-energy or layer-cake argument is needed for this refinement.

For \(t>0\), at least one term defining \(\Psi(t)\) is positive, while the terms are bounded by \(t^2/k\) and tend to zero as \(k\to\infty\). Any chosen positive term exceeds every sufficiently late term, so the maximum is taken among a finite set. At \(t=0\), all terms are zero. There are finitely many nonempty classes, and their integers \(k_b\) in (24) can be chosen independently to attain their respective maxima. Dividing by \(3W>0\) proves \(K(w)\ge(W/6)\sum_b\Psi(\pi_b)\).

For the collision consequence, set \(k_b^*:=1+\lceil\log_2(1/\pi_b)\rceil\) for each nonempty class. These are positive integers, \(2^{-k_b^*}\le\pi_b/2\), and \(k_b^*\le2+\log_2(1/\pi_b)\). Therefore \(\Psi(\pi_b)\ge\pi_b^2/(4k_b^*)\). Put \(r_b:=\pi_b^2/q\) on the nonempty classes. Both \((r_b)\) and \((\pi_b)\) are positive probability vectors on this set. The elementary inequality \(\log u\le u-1\) gives
\[
\sum_b r_b\log\frac{\pi_b}{r_b}
\le\sum_b r_b\left(\frac{\pi_b}{r_b}-1\right)=0.
\]
Rearranging and using \(r_b/\pi_b=\pi_b/q\) yields \(\sum_b r_b\log\pi_b\ge\log q\). Consequently,
\[
\sum_b r_b k_b^*
\le2+\sum_b r_b\log_2(1/\pi_b)
\le2+\log_2(1/q).
\tag{25}
\]
Cauchy-Schwarz applied to \(\sqrt{r_b/k_b^*}\) and \(\sqrt{r_bk_b^*}\) now gives
\[
\sum_b\Psi(\pi_b)
\ge\frac q4\sum_b\frac{r_b}{k_b^*}
\ge\frac{q}{4\sum_b r_bk_b^*}
\ge\frac{q}{4(2+\log_2(1/q))}.
\tag{26}
\]
Here \(q>0\); also Cauchy-Schwarz gives \(q\ge2^{-n}\), and \(\pi_b^2\le\pi_b\) gives \(q\le1\).

Each function \(t\mapsto(t-2^{-k})_+^2/k\) is convex. Its supremum \(\Psi\) is therefore convex. Applying Jensen's inequality to all \(2^n\) parity classes, including empty ones, gives
\[
\sum_b\Psi(\pi_b)
\ge2^n\Psi(2^{-n})
\ge2^n\frac{(2^{-n}-2^{-(n+1)})^2}{n+1}
=\frac1{4(n+1)2^n}.
\tag{27}
\]
This proves the rest of (3), and recovers the exact scalar constant from `03f071403cdfc69f`. In the exactly balanced case every term with \(k\le n\) vanishes; extracting \(2^{-2n}\) from the other terms proves the identity in (13). The choice \(k=n+1\) gives its lower bound. For every \(k\ge n+1\), its numerator is at most one and its denominator at least \(n+1\), giving its upper bound. These bounds concern the optimized expression itself.

We now apply the harmonic bound to the two support geometries. The exact census in `032423921efad6c8` gives \(2^{n_{m,Q}}\eta_m^s\) points at level \(s\), and \(0<\eta_m<1\). Thus
\[
\frac{|A_{m,Q}|}{2^{n_{m,Q}}}
=\sum_{s=0}^Q\eta_m^s\le Q+1.
\tag{28}
\]
For a table supported on a subset, \(N_A\) is no larger. Substituting into (3) proves (7), regardless of its new weights. If \(m\ge2\), then \(n_{m,Q}\ge m^Q\ge2^Q\), so \(Q\le\log_2 n_{m,Q}\), proving the stated replacement. If \(m=1\), then \(\eta_1=1/2\), and the sum in (28) is strictly less than two, giving the constant-loss bound.

For the lifted supports, the exact column description is supplied by `604889294a17d7df`, with its \(N\) replaced by \(D=n_{m,Q}+1\). It and the same level census give
\[
\frac{|\widehat A|}{2^D}
=\frac12\sum_{s=0}^Q\eta_m^s(k-a_s+1)
\le\frac{k+1}{2}(Q+1).
\tag{29}
\]
The profile condition implies \(\rho_\ell\le2^{-\ell}\). The sequence \(2^\ell/(8\ell)\) is increasing for integers \(\ell\ge8\) and equals four at eight. Hence
\[
b_\ell\ge\left\lfloor\frac{2^\ell}{8\ell}\right\rfloor\ge4
\quad(8\le\ell\le k),
\qquad
Q\ge4(k-7)\ge k/2.
\tag{30}
\]
The last inequality is equivalent to \(k\ge8\), so it holds also at the smallest allowed value. Thus \((k+1)(Q+1)/2\le(Q+1)^2\). The support inequality in (3), now in dimension \(D\), proves the first bound in (9) for every admissible new table. Since \(m\ge2\) and \(D\ge m^Q\ge2^Q\), it proves the second as well.

For the uniform logarithmic-dimension conclusions, \(n_{m,Q}\ge Q\), so (28) implies \(N_A/2^{n_{m,Q}}\le n_{m,Q}+1\le n_{m,Q}+2\). In the lifted case \(D\ge Q+1\), so (29)-(30) give normalized support at most \((Q+1)^2\le(D+2)^2\). Apply (4) with \(a=1\) and \(a=2\), respectively. This gives fixed positive lower bounds for the normalized expression on the left of (5), excluding a sequence tending to zero even without assuming increasing dimensions.

For the stronger divergence claim in growing dimension, when \(m\ge2\) the original-tree expression is bounded below by
\[
\frac{\log(n+2)}{3\left(1+\tfrac12\log(1+\log_2 n)\right)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{31}
\]
When \(m=1\), its denominator can instead be replaced by the fixed number \(3(1+\tfrac12\log2)\), giving the same conclusion. These bounds also handle sequences switching between the two cases, since both lower bounds tend to infinity with \(n\). The lifted expression is bounded below by \(\log(D+2)/[3(1+\log(1+\log_2 D))]\), which tends to infinity. The limits follow, for example, from \(\log x/x\to0\) as \(x\to\infty\), applied to \(x=\log(n+2)\) or \(x=\log(D+2)\).

It remains to verify the new exact calibration (11). From `032423921efad6c8`, \(P_{m,Q}\cap\mathbb Z^{n_{m,Q}}=A_{m,Q}\) and \(P_{m,Q}\subseteq[0,2]^{n_{m,Q}}\), with \([0,1]^{n_{m,Q}}\subseteq P_{m,Q}\). The function \(\rho_{m,Q}\) in (10) is the minimum of finitely many affine functions, hence is continuous and concave. Each affine entry is at least \(1/(Q+1)\) on the ternary box, while the entry one bounds the minimum above. Thus \(1/(Q+1)\le\rho_{m,Q}\le1\). At a level-\(s\) lattice point the coordinates equal to two occur precisely at depths \(1,\ldots,s\); they contribute \(1/(\ell+1)\), and all other coordinates contribute at least one. Therefore \(\rho_{m,Q}(z)=1/(s+1)\).

These affine upper bounds and \(y\ge0\) define the compact convex polytope \(C_{m,Q}\). It contains \([0,1]^{n_{m,Q}}\times[0,1]\), so it is full-dimensional and has exactly the asserted interval fibers and all the asserted zero fibers. Concavity and the weighted arithmetic-geometric mean inequality show that the function equal to \(\rho_{m,Q}\) on \(P_{m,Q}\) and zero outside is globally log-concave. When an endpoint is outside \(P_{m,Q}\), the zero-endpoint convention makes that inequality immediate; when both are inside, their segment stays in the convex support. This checks the actual-volume and extension interpretation of the accepted example with the normalization used here.

Use the complete pair reconstruction in `032423921efad6c8`. At a center \(j\) of level \(s\), the unordered distinct pairs are precisely one pair for every \(s<t\le s+h_-(j)\), with endpoint levels \(s,t\). There are no others; \(h_-(j)\) is that fact's inverse-reconstruction length. Their minimum weight is \(1/(t+1)\), and their curvature is \(\log((t+1)/(s+1))\). The zero displacement has weight \(1/(s+1)\) and curvature zero. Consequently
\[
B_j^\Delta(L)
=\frac1{s+1}
+2\sum_{\substack{s<t\le s+h_-(j)\\t+1\le(s+1)e^L}}\frac1{t+1}.
\tag{32}
\]
If this sum is nonempty and \(T\) is its largest index, the index set is consecutive and
\[
\sum_{t=s+1}^{T}\frac1{t+1}
\le\int_{s+1}^{T+1}\frac{du}{u}
=\log\frac{T+1}{s+1}\le L.
\]
If it is empty, the same bound is immediate. Thus \(B_j^\Delta(L)\le1+2L\) for every center and cutoff, and \(K_Q\le2\). The accepted reconstruction also gives exactly one unordered pair at the all-ones center for each level \(t=1,\ldots,Q\). This center has level zero. At \(L=\log(Q+1)\), (32) there equals \(1+2\sum_{t=1}^Q1/(t+1)=2H_{Q+1}-1\), proving the lower bound for \(K_Q\) in (11).

For completeness, put \(\delta_Q:=1-\eta_{m_Q}\). The elementary central-binomial estimate proved in `032423921efad6c8` gives \(0<\delta_Q<1/(Q+1)^2\). Its exact level census and the weights just checked give
\[
\tau_Q=\sum_{s=0}^Q(1-\delta_Q)^s,
\qquad
\frac{W_Q}{2^{n_Q}}=\sum_{s=0}^Q\frac{(1-\delta_Q)^s}{s+1}.
\tag{33}
\]
Bernoulli's inequality now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_Q
&\ge Q+1-\delta_Q\frac{Q(Q+1)}2
>Q+\tfrac12,\\
\frac{W_Q}{2^{n_Q}}
&\ge H_{Q+1}-\delta_Q\bigl((Q+1)-H_{Q+1}\bigr)
>H_{Q+1}-\frac1{Q+1}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{34}
\]
The upper bounds \(\tau_Q<Q+1\) and \(W_Q/2^{n_Q}\le H_{Q+1}\) follow directly from \(0<1-\delta_Q<1\). The elementary harmonic estimates \(\log(r+1)\le H_r\le1+\log r\) imply \(H_{Q+1}\sim\log Q\). The lower and upper score bounds therefore squeeze \(K_Q\) to two, and (33)-(34) give \(W_Q/2^{n_Q}\sim\log Q\) and \(\log\tau_Q\sim\log Q\).

Exact geometric summation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
n_Q&=m_Q^Q\frac{1-m_Q^{-Q}}{1-m_Q^{-1}},\\
\log n_Q
&=Q\log m_Q+\log(1-m_Q^{-Q})-\log(1-m_Q^{-1}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{35}
\]
Since \(m_Q\to\infty\), the last two logarithms tend to zero. Also \(\log m_Q=\log2+4\log(Q+1)\), so \(\log n_Q\sim4Q\log Q\). Adding two to \(n_Q\) changes its logarithm by \(o(1)\). Taking another logarithm gives
\[
\log\log(n_Q+2)
=\log Q+\log\log Q+\log4+o(1)
\sim\log Q.
\tag{36}
\]
Multiplying these asymptotics by \(K_Q/(W_Q/2^{n_Q})\sim2/\log Q\) proves all three normalized-score limits in (11), including the constant \(8\) in its last line.

To state sharpness precisely, if \(g(t)>0\) for all sufficiently large \(t\) and \(g(t)=o(\log t)\), then (11) implies \(g(\tau_Q)2^{n_Q}K_Q/W_Q\to0\). Hence no fixed \(c>0\) can give \(K(w)\ge cW/[2^n g(N_A/2^n)]\) on all these actual tables. If instead \(g(n)>0\) eventually and \(g(n)=o(\log\log(n+2))\), the second normalized limit in (11) gives the same contradiction to \(K(w)\ge cW/[2^ng(n)]\). The last limit in (11) shows explicitly why this family does not refute a logarithmic dimension loss.

Finally, accepted fact `03f071403cdfc69f` proves that every positive actual fiber-volume table satisfies the midpoint hypothesis, and that its attained canonical score supplies one point \(p^\star\in S\) with \(h_S(p^\star)\ge K(w)/12\). Its construction fixes the integer center, curvature cutoff, and continuous point before choosing the containing closed ambient halfspace, and includes vertical halfspaces and boundaries containing whole fibers. Apply that exact statement to the definitions in (1). Combining it with (3) proves (12), including the unchanged coefficient \(1/[288(n+1)]\). Dividing (4) and every other scalar lower bound by twelve is valid for the same selected point because each is a lower bound on that one numerical maximum \(K(w)\). If \(W=0\), nonnegativity of mixed volume makes the required zero bound immediate at any point in the assumed nonempty \(S\).
statement:
Let \(n\ge1\) be an integer and let \(w=(w_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\) be a nonzero, nonnegative, finitely supported table of finite real numbers. Put \(A:=\{z:w_z>0\}\), \(W:=\sum_z w_z>0\), and \(N_A:=|A|\). Assume that whenever \(x,y\in A\) have the same coordinatewise parity, \(w_{(x+y)/2}^2\ge w_xw_y\). This implies positivity of the integer midpoint. No global log-concave extension is required. All logarithms are natural unless a base two is displayed; put \(\log_+ t:=\max\{0,\log t\}\) for \(t>0\) and \((u)_+:=\max\{u,0\}\). The symbol \(N_A\) is the support count denoted by \(N\) in the motivating logarithmic-loss transcript. In the lifted-tree application below, \(D\) is exactly the integer dimension denoted by \(N\) in accepted fact `604889294a17d7df`; these quantities are kept distinct.

Retain the displayed-center notation and normalization of accepted fact `c382ad0f37a86dd8`: for \(j\in A\), let \(\alpha_j(v):=\min\{w_{j+v},w_{j-v}\}\), \(\mathcal U_j:=\{v\in\mathbb Z^n:\alpha_j(v)>0\}\), and \(\Delta_j(v):=\log(w_j^2/(w_{j+v}w_{j-v}))\) for \(v\in\mathcal U_j\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
B_j^\Delta(L)&:=\sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal U_j\\\Delta_j(v)\le L}}\alpha_j(v)
&& (L\ge0),\\
K_j(w)&:=\max_{L\ge0}\frac{B_j^\Delta(L)}{1+L},
&K(w)&:=\max_{j\in A}K_j(w),\\
E_j&:=\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_j}\alpha_j(v)e^{-\Delta_j(v)/2},
&\mathscr R&:=\sum_{j\in A}w_jE_j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
Every displacement sum is oriented and includes zero. The maxima in (1) are attained. In particular, \(E_j\) and \(\mathscr R\) have exactly their discounted meanings in `c382ad0f37a86dd8`.

For \(b\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^n\), put \(R_b:=|\{z\in A:z\equiv b\pmod2\}|\), \(W_b:=\sum_{z\equiv b\pmod2}w_z\), \(\pi_b:=W_b/W\), and \(q:=\sum_b\pi_b^2\). Thus \(W_b\) and \(q\) agree with `c382ad0f37a86dd8`; \(q\in[2^{-n},1]\) is a parity-collision probability. In each nonempty class arrange its positive weights as \(a_{b,1}\ge\cdots\ge a_{b,R_b}>0\), and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathscr H(A)&:=\sum_{b:R_b>0}\sum_{r=1}^{R_b}\frac1{2r-1},\\
\Psi(t)&:=\max_{k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}}\frac{(t-2^{-k})_+^2}{k}
\quad(0\le t\le1).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The maximum defining \(\Psi\) is attained, including at \(t=0\). Every table above satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
K(w)
&\ge\frac1{3W}\sum_{b:R_b>0}\sum_{r=1}^{R_b}(2r-1)a_{b,r}^2
\ge\frac{W}{3\mathscr H(A)}\\
&\ge\frac{W}{3\,2^n\left(1+\tfrac12\log_+(N_A/2^n)\right)},\\
K(w)&\ge\frac W6\sum_b\Psi(\pi_b),\\
\sum_b\Psi(\pi_b)
&\ge\max\left\{
\frac{q}{4\left(2+\log_2(1/q)\right)},
\frac1{4(n+1)2^n}
\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
In particular, the optimized parity bound always implies the unchanged universal bound \(K(w)\ge W/[24(n+1)2^n]\) of `03f071403cdfc69f`.

For each fixed real \(a\ge0\), every table above with \(N_A/2^n\le(n+2)^a\) satisfies
\[
K(w)\ge c_a\frac{W}{2^n\log(n+2)},
\qquad
c_a:=\frac1{3\left((\log3)^{-1}+a/2\right)}.
\tag{4}
\]
For any sequence of finite tables satisfying the midpoint hypothesis above, with integer dimensions \(n_i\), positive total weights \(W_i\), and \(\tau_i:=|\operatorname{supp}w^{(i)}|/2^{n_i}\), one has the necessary implication
\[
\log(n_i+2)\frac{2^{n_i}K(w^{(i)})}{W_i}\longrightarrow0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\frac{\log_+\tau_i}{\log(n_i+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{5}
\]
The conclusion implies \(\tau_i/(n_i+2)^a\to\infty\) for every fixed \(a\ge0\).

The following two support applications allow arbitrary new weights satisfying the stated midpoint hypothesis, including tables whose positive support is a proper subset of the specified support. No symmetry by tree level or monotonicity of the new weights is imposed.

For integers \(m,Q\ge1\), use exactly the rooted-tree sets \(A_{m,Q}\), hulls \(P_{m,Q}\), and levels of accepted fact `032423921efad6c8`. More explicitly, their coordinates are indexed by \(\mathcal T_{m,Q}:=\bigcup_{\ell=1}^Q[m]^\ell\), where \([m]:=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Choose a partition of \(\{0,1\}^m\) into symmetric saturated chains. Let \(D_m\) be its nonterminal patterns and \(F_m\) the chain-successor map, with \(F_m(c)=c+e_{i_m(c)}\) for \(c\in D_m\). Here \(e_i\) is a coordinate unit vector in a Boolean block, \(e_u\) is a coordinate unit vector in the full tree space, and \(b[u]:=(b_{u1},\ldots,b_{um})\) is the child block at \(u\). For a global Boolean vector \(b\), start at the root and, at a node \(u\), follow the child \(u i_m(b[u])\) if its child block \(b[u]\) is in \(D_m\). Stop otherwise or at depth \(Q\). If the resulting path is \(u_1,\ldots,u_{h(b)}\), then
\[
\begin{aligned}
n_{m,Q}&:=\sum_{\ell=1}^Qm^\ell,
&\eta_m&:=1-2^{-m}\binom m{\lfloor m/2\rfloor},\\
z_s(b)&:=b+2\sum_{\ell=1}^s e_{u_\ell},
&A_{m,Q}&:=\{z_s(b):0\le s\le h(b)\},
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
where the union in \(A_{m,Q}\) is over all global Boolean \(b\), and the level of \(z_s(b)\) is \(s\). Put \(P_{m,Q}:=\operatorname{conv}(A_{m,Q})\). The existence of the chain partition and the support properties used below are accepted in `032423921efad6c8`.

Every table satisfying the scalar hypotheses in dimension \(n=n_{m,Q}\), with \(A\subseteq A_{m,Q}\), obeys
\[
K(w)\ge\frac{W}{3\,2^n\left(1+\tfrac12\log(Q+1)\right)}.
\tag{7}
\]
When \(m\ge2\), one may replace \(\log(Q+1)\) in (7) by \(\log(1+\log_2 n)\). When \(m=1\), the stronger bound \(K(w)\ge W/[3\,2^n(1+\tfrac12\log2)]\) holds.

For the lifted supports, take an integer \(k\ge8\) and a profile \(\rho_0,\ldots,\rho_k>0\) with \(\rho_0=1\) and \(\rho_{t+1}\le\rho_t/2\). Retain the geometry parameters of `604889294a17d7df`: let \(b_\ell=0\) for \(1\le\ell<8\), let \(b_\ell:=\lfloor1/(8\ell\rho_\ell)\rfloor\) for \(8\le\ell\le k\), let \(Q_0=0\), \(Q_\ell:=\sum_{r=1}^\ell b_r\), and \(Q:=Q_k\). Define \(a_0=0\), and \(a_s=\ell\) when \(Q_{\ell-1}<s\le Q_\ell\). Set \(m:=2(Q+1)^4\) and \(D:=n_{m,Q}+1\), and define the same exact lifted lattice support as that predecessor by
\[
\widehat A:=\{(z,t):z\in A_{m,Q},\ a_{\operatorname{level}(z)}\le t\le k,\ t\in\mathbb Z\}
\subseteq\mathbb Z^D.
\tag{8}
\]
Here \(D\) is the predecessor's \(N\), and \(n_{m,Q}\) is its \(n\). The profile \(\rho_t\) determines this geometry and need not be the profile of the new table. Every nonzero table satisfying the scalar hypotheses in dimension \(D\), with positive support contained in \(\widehat A\), satisfies
\[
K(w)\ge\frac{W}{3\,2^D(1+\log(Q+1))}
\ge\frac{W}{3\,2^D\left(1+\log(1+\log_2 D)\right)}.
\tag{9}
\]
Consequently all admissible reweightings of (6) satisfy (4) with \(a=1\), and all admissible reweightings of (8) satisfy its dimension-\(D\) version with \(a=2\). Neither support family can yield a sequence on the left of (5). More strongly, along either family with its integer dimension tending to infinity, the left-hand expression in (5), with that dimension substituted, tends to infinity.

The support dependence and the dimension rate have the following exact calibration. For every \(Q\ge1\), put \(m_Q:=2(Q+1)^4\), \(n_Q:=n_{m_Q,Q}\), and \(A_Q:=A_{m_Q,Q}\). On \(P_{m,Q}\) define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{m,Q}(x)&:=
\min\left\{1,\ \min_{u\in\mathcal T_{m,Q}}
\left[1-\frac{|u|}{|u|+1}(x_u-1)\right]\right\},\\
C_{m,Q}&:=\{(x,y):x\in P_{m,Q},\ 0\le y\le\rho_{m,Q}(x)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
The function \(\rho_{m,Q}(x)\) is exactly the interval-height function \(\rho(x)\) of `032423921efad6c8`, with its parameters displayed; it is distinct from the discrete profile \(\rho_t\) used in (8). The body \(C_{m,Q}\) is that predecessor's full-dimensional convex polytope with continuous dimension one. Its actual interval-fiber table gives weight \(1/(s+1)\) to each level-\(s\) point of \(A_{m,Q}\), and zero elsewhere, and has a global log-concave extension agreeing at all integer zeros. Let \(w^{[Q]}\) be this table for \(m=m_Q\), and put \(K_Q:=K(w^{[Q]})\), \(W_Q:=\sum_z w_z^{[Q]}\), \(\tau_Q:=|A_Q|/2^{n_Q}\), and \(H_r:=\sum_{s=1}^r1/s\) for integers \(r\ge1\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{2H_{Q+1}-1}{1+\log(Q+1)}&\le K_Q\le2,
\qquad K_Q\longrightarrow2,\\
H_{Q+1}-\frac1{Q+1}&<\frac{W_Q}{2^{n_Q}}\le H_{Q+1},\\
Q+\tfrac12&<\tau_Q<Q+1,\\
\log n_Q&=Q\log m_Q+o(1)\sim4Q\log Q,\\
\log\tau_Q\frac{2^{n_Q}K_Q}{W_Q}&\longrightarrow2,\\
\log\log(n_Q+2)\frac{2^{n_Q}K_Q}{W_Q}&\longrightarrow2,\\
\log(n_Q+2)\frac{2^{n_Q}K_Q}{W_Q}&\sim8Q\longrightarrow\infty.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
All limits are as \(Q\to\infty\). Thus the logarithmic loss in \(N_A/2^n\) in (3) cannot be replaced uniformly by any positive loss function \(o(\log(N_A/2^n))\), even for actual interval-fiber tables. Likewise every proposed scalar loss \(o(\log\log(n+2))\) fails on this same family. These are statements about \(K\), not upper bounds on actual halfspace depth.

For the actual-body consequence, let \(n,d\ge1\) and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body with nonempty \(S:=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\). Define \(C_z:=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}\), \(w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)\), and \(W:=\sum_z w_z=\mathcal H_d(S)\), assigning zero volume to empty or lower-dimensional fibers. Let \(h_S(p):=\inf_{H\ni p}\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\), over closed ambient halfspaces. If \(W>0\), there is one \(p^\star\in S\), fixed before the halfspace, with \(h_S(p^\star)\ge K(w)/12\). Therefore every scalar lower bound above, divided by twelve, holds for that same point. In particular,
\[
\begin{aligned}
h_S(p^\star)&\ge\frac{W}{36\,2^n\left(1+\tfrac12\log_+(N_A/2^n)\right)},\\
h_S(p^\star)&\ge\frac W{72}\sum_b\Psi(\pi_b)
\ge\frac{Wq}{288\left(2+\log_2(1/q)\right)},\\
h_S(p^\star)&\ge\frac{W}{288(n+1)2^n}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
Here \(N_A\) counts positive-volume integer fibers. If \(W=0\), any point of \(S\) satisfies the zero lower bound, and none of the positive-table normalizations is needed.

For exactly balanced parities, \(\pi_b=2^{-n}\) for every \(b\), the optimized band expression in (12) is precisely
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac W{72}\sum_b\Psi(\pi_b)
&=\frac{2^{-n}W}{72}\max_{k\ge n+1}\frac{(1-2^{n-k})^2}{k},\\
\frac1{4(n+1)}
&\le\max_{k\ge n+1}\frac{(1-2^{n-k})^2}{k}\le\frac1{n+1}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
The maxima in (13) are over integers. Thus this particular certificate still has a coefficient of order \(1/n\). Formula (13) is not an upper bound on \(K(w)\) or on the body's depth. No unrestricted dimension-only logarithmic bound for \(K(w)\) follows from the claims above.
